requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: firewalld was active and enabled before restart, the reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and the system recovered with firewalld still active and enabled and the intended runtime and permanent policy intact. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently confirm the restart.

requirements.requirement: Permit inbound SSH and TCP port 8080.
requirements.summary: Both runtime and permanent firewalld policy allow SSH and 8080/tcp. The active nftables allow chain accepts TCP ports 22 and 8080, and SSH remained active and listening after reboot.

The active public zone has a REJECT target, exposes only SSH and 8080/tcp, and its nftables chain ends with an admin-prohibited rejection after the intended allow rules. This state persisted across reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied. node1 has a persistent firewalld policy that allows SSH and TCP/8080 and rejects other public-zone inbound traffic. The mandatory restart protocol is complete and coherent: healthy pre-state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered system, firewall, SSH service, listeners, and rules.
limitations: No external packet-level connection tests were captured for ports 22, 8080, or an unrelated port; the assessment relies on direct runtime/permanent firewalld state, generated nftables rules, and post-reboot recovery observations.
No service was listening on TCP/8080, so application-level reachability on that port could not be demonstrated; the firewall allowance itself is directly shown.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed mutations had a clear task or verification role: removing unrelated allowances and adding the required port and REJECT target, reloading the firewall, and performing the mandatory restart. No unnecessary mutation was identified, no failed services or package damage remained, and temporary-file differences were normal reboot-created systemd private directories.
